scope: Publish exact source/results bytes with bounded, reconstructible JSON chunks.

summary.scope: Matched full-arm rigid/deformable contact feedback, native nodal replay and fixed-law temporal diagnostics

temporal_audit.scope: Audit common-time full-arm contact fields with one unchanged closed initial state.
temporal_audit.limitations: All steps retain complete original1e-9 body/joint/fresh-step budgets and common closure arrays. This tests the declared short hold with zero initial velocity at one coarse fixed-polyhedron/contact setting. It does not establish original approach/lift/angular-history matching, spatial/contact/regularization convergence, resolved-load/native feedback separation or a physical accuracy/cost range.

rigid_pilot.scope: Solve a rigid-egg counterpart of the declared full-arm deformable-contact hold.
rigid_pilot.limitations: Rigid-body motion restricts the same collision surface and consistent mass, preserving actual robot control/contact laws. Body rotational residuals are scaled by the fixed reference radius only in the numerical merit. Raw force/moment and fresh robot-step gates are explicit. This short held-initializer/zero-velocity control is not original approach/angular-history matching or spatial/contact/regularization convergence. Independent balance/recovery replay and rigid/deformable feedback comparisons are required.

feedback_audit.scope: Independently audit matched rigid/deformable holds and replay their resolved body loads.
feedback_audit.limitations: The same geometry/control/contact/mass with rigid versus deformable body motion isolates feedback within the declared short held-initializer protocol. Initial equilibria are solved separately under the same supports/targets, not artificially forced to have identical loads. Linear full-inertia replay separates resolved-load changes from nonlinear constitutive effects. Native recovery, finite-footprint mapping, original approach/angular history, spatial/contact/regularization tails and physical accuracy/cost remain unverified here.

native_replay.scope: Replay independently audited rigid/deformable body loads through actual native recovery.
native_replay.limitations: Actual native nodal replay isolates elastic algebra and compares full-inertia versus rigid-relief inputs at declared sampled times. It does not qualify finite-footprint mapping, contact/spatial/regularization convergence, original approach/angular history or physically verified warmed cost. Rigid/deformable feedback comes from independently solved corresponding contact histories, not native algebra agreement.

checks: Readable at intended width; no clipped labels or legend/data overlap.
Colour and line-style/marker redundancy distinguish curves.
All240 deterministic source samples retained; no fitted order, smoothing or statistical bands.
Axes identify percent and milliseconds; logarithmic y axes remain explicit.
figure_qa.limitations: Only one unresolved480-tet/contact setting and a short held-initializer history.

failures: Rigid pilot v1/v2 fail the unchanged1e-3 directional-tangent gate at perturbations1e-9/1e-10. The complete accepted64-target held state and source/logs are retained. The extended perturbation sequence reaches2.625e-4/4.284e-4 at1e-11 without changing the gate or physical law.

limitations: Temporal and resolved-contact feedback are qualified only for the declared short hold at one coarse spatial/contact setting. Original approach/lift/angular history, spatial/contact/regularization tails, Genesis contact-law equivalence, finite-footprint model mapping and physically verified warmed costs remain incomplete. Exact successes and failed diagnostics are retained. Earlier deformable/capture inputs remain in the named immutable dependency. JSON files above200MB are preserved as exact ordered32MiB byte ranges, individually gzip-compressed, with original/part/stored SHA256 and offsets. Join decompressed ranges in index order to restore the original JSON exactly; no records are reduced or excluded. Runtime staging uses hard links for unchanged small originals.
